Subject: Re: SIG follow-up — encryption evidence and key lifecycle

John — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers you can paste into the SIG (I’ve included proposed wording per field). I attached a ZIP with three files: key_management_policy_v2.pdf, rotation_log_redacted.csv, and a short evidence summary PDF. Drive link included at the bottom.

1) Encryption in transit (SIG field: "in-transit encryption"):
Redwood enforces TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 preferred) on all external and internal RPCs. External client traffic to Redwood endpoints is secured with TLS and certificate pinning for our public APIs. Inter-service communication within our hosted environment uses mutual TLS and network-level isolation.

2) Encryption at rest (SIG field: "at-rest encryption"):
Customer data and model artifacts are encrypted at rest using envelope encryption. Data encryption keys (DEKs) are generated per-tenant and encrypted (wrapped) with a higher-level master key (CMK). All persistent storage (object stores, databases, caches at rest) is encrypted with DEKs.

3) KMS / HSM usage (SIG field: "key management"):
- Hosted (Redwood-managed): CMKs are created and managed in AWS KMS; production CMKs are backed by dedicated CloudHSM clusters for HSM protection of key material.
- Dedicated / Private deployments: customers may provision their own KMS (BYOK) using CloudHSM or an on-prem HSM; Redwood can accept an externally managed CMK or integrate via standard KMS APIs.
- We support both service-managed and customer-managed CMKs. When customers provide their own CMK, Redwood uses it for wrapping/unwrapping DEKs but does not retain plaintext master keys.

4) Key rotation policy (SIG field: "key rotation lcm"):
- Data encryption keys (DEKs): rotated automatically every 90 days by default; shorter cadences configurable per-customer. DEKs used for short-lived caches are rotated more frequently (24h) depending on workload.
- Master/wrapper keys (CMKs): default automatic rotation is enabled annually for Redwood-managed CMKs; customers who BYOK control their own CMK rotation schedule.
- All rotations are logged; rotation events include key id, timestamp, initiating principal, and a rotation digest. We can provide redacted rotation logs for audit requests (see attached rotation_log_redacted.csv).

5) Access controls and separation of duties:
Key material is only accessible to a small set of KMS/HSM service agents. Production HSM clusters are isolated, and operators do not have access to plaintext DEKs. Administrative operations (rotate, revoke) require multi-person approval for private deployments when configured.

Attachments included in ZIP: key_management_policy_v2.pdf (policy and procedure), rotation_log_redacted.csv (sample, redacted), SIG_Encryption_Evidence_summary.pdf (one-page answers + references).

Drive upload: https://drive.redwood.com/sig/acme/2026/SIG_Encryption_Evidence.zip

If you want, I can also provide a short extract for the SIG: "Redwood uses envelope encryption: tenant-specific DEKs are rotated every 90 days and wrapped with HSM-backed CMKs (CloudHSM for hosted deployments). Customer-managed keys (BYOK) are supported; rotation and access events are logged and available for audit."

Let me know which specific SIG question numbers you want that extract pasted into; happy to supply.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen

Stephanie / Priyom — a couple of quick notes to tighten the response before shipping: 

- For the SIG checkbox that asks "Are CMKs HSM-backed?": say explicitly "Yes — Redwood-managed production CMKs are backed by dedicated CloudHSM clusters (Amazon CloudHSM)." Avoid saying "HSM-backed when possible."
- Provide one example rotation row in the CSV with only date, key-id prefix, and rotation actor; redact anything that could be tenant-identifying.
- Add one line on our envelope encryption implementation: cite libraries/agents (we use libcrypto-based key wrapping with AEAD for DEKs — avoid internal repo names).
- For Private deployments note: customers can elect to keep CMKs entirely in their HSM and Redwood will only call the KMS endpoints; include that as a sentence.

Attached to this internal draft: rotation_log_redacted.csv (sample), suggested paste for SIG Qs 3.2.1 and 3.2.2: 

"Redwood performs envelope encryption for all customer data. DEKs are rotated by default every 90 days; CMKs used to wrap DEKs are HSM-backed in hosted deployments and may be customer-managed in Private deployments. Rotation events are logged and available as redacted CSV export for audit."

If you want, Priyom can paste that into the SIG and upload the ZIP.

- Vivek

Q: "How is data encrypted in transit?"
A: "All external and internal RPCs enforce TLS 1.2 or higher; external API endpoints require TLS with certificate validation. Internal service-to-service communication uses mutual TLS and network isolation."

Q: "How is data encrypted at rest and how are keys managed?"
A: "Redwood uses envelope encryption: per-tenant data encryption keys (DEKs) protect data at rest. DEKs are wrapped with HSM-backed CMKs. Hosted Redwood-managed CMKs are backed by dedicated CloudHSM clusters; customers may provide BYOK CMKs for Dedicated/Private deployments. DEKs rotate by default every 90 days (shorter cadences configurable); CMK rotation is typically annual for Redwood-managed keys but is customer-controlled for BYOK. Rotation events are recorded and available for audit in redacted form."
